blind_alternative: writes no sidecar at all and rebuilds everything from responses_0.jsonl on every load, since the append-only log is self-describing and a second file is a second thing that can be wrong
writes the checkpoint once at the end of run() (or on the stop_tracker path), one write instead of N, which is what 'checkpoint' usually means
treats the persisted cursor as the authority and truncates or ignores log lines beyond it, the usual resumable-writer pattern since the cursor is written after a successful append

either raises on a missing or unreadable sidecar (treating absence as corruption) or silently rebuilds from the log in all mismatch cases, with no TurnLedgerDesyncError and no per-arm status vocabulary

if a sidecar is written at all, uses model_dump_json() or json.dumps with default separators and insertion order, a different filename, a different key set, and no version field — so no byte-exact content and no desync attributes to assert on
leaves is_completed returning False as a pure subclass hook (today's body, which the ticket does not ask to change), or invents a different token such as '[END]', '<END>', 'TERMINATE' or 'DONE'
documents 'agent_signal' as reachable only for user-written Agent subclasses, leaving the base class with no protocol token at all

uses a substring test anywhere in the message, compares case-insensitively, lets a non-str response_message raise (or coerces it with str() first), and/or drops the terminating message from the log or the dataset as a control signal rather than content

an end-to-end run in which the fake is called max_length times and the log reaches max_length + 1 lines because nothing ever signals completion, with completion_reason 'budget' instead of 'agent_signal'
